precepts.text: O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites. He is calling us the dead Israelites. We are not physically dead, but spiritually we are a dead race of people: filled with hatred, filled with adulteries, pornography, drug dealing, drug abuse. We hate each other and cannot get along. That is why it calls us the dead Israelites.
precepts.point: And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city. What is the biblical name of the great city?

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Who are the dead bodies lying in the street of the great city? Baruch names them: “O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites”. He is calling us the dead Israelites.

We are not physically dead, but spiritually we are a dead race of people: filled with hatred, filled with adulteries, filled with pornography; some child molesters, drug dealers, drug users, drug abusers. We hate each other and can't get along. That is why it calls us the dead Israelites.

So Revelation 11:8 is speaking of us: the dead Israelites whose bodies lie in the street of Babylon the great, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.

precepts.text: He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved. That is the holy and beloved.
precepts.point: The Lord through the apostle Paul is instructing the Colossians on how to deal with one another: bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering, forbearing one another and forgiving one another. Why? Because we are the same people. We are the sons and daughters of the living God, so there is a way we have to govern ourselves and treat each other.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Holy, and beloved. Baruch shows who the beloved is: “He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” Israel is his beloved, and it is to Israel he gave all the way of knowledge.

So the “holy and beloved” of Colossians 3:12 are the children of Israel: holy because he severed them from other people, beloved because he calls Israel his beloved.

That is why the Lord, through the apostle Paul, instructs the Colossians on how to deal with one another: “bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another”. Why? Because we are the same people. We are the sons and daughters of the living God, and there is a way we have to govern ourselves and treat each other.

precepts.text: There were the giants famous from the beginning, of so great stature and so expert in war: the offspring of the sons of God. Those did not the Lord choose; they were destroyed because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness. How were they destroyed? The flood.
precepts.point: After the Most High sent the flood, those same spirits came right back through the three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. There is no new thing under the sun.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Baruch says the same thing as Genesis 6: “There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war.” Those giants were the offspring of the sons of God, the mighty men of renown, and they were expert in war as well.

“Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them.” God did not choose them; they were wicked. “But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.” How were they destroyed? The flood. God saw that “every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually,” and he wiped it out.

But those same spirits came right back, by way of the three sons of Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth. There is no new thing under the sun. Jude speaks of “certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation,” the same words, “of old,” that Genesis 6 uses of the men of renown. The same kind of wickedness is still here, reserved “unto the judgment of the great day,” which has not yet come.

So the giants are not a fantasy of fallen angels, the Nephilim Esau talks about. They were men, the offspring of the sons of God, who had no wisdom, and whose spirit lives on until the judgment.

precepts.text: O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites. When we sin against God, God refers to us as dead; remember the scripture says keep my commandments and live. For which cause these plagues cleave unto us: one of those plagues is us going into slavery on ships, one of the curses of Deuteronomy 28.
precepts.point: The great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt: the same spirit that was in Sodom and Gomorrah, all that filth, is the same spirit here in America; and the same spirit that was in ancient Egypt, the oppression of the Israelites, is the same spirit here in America. That is why this place is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”. The “their” is the Israelites. Why does it call us dead bodies? Baruch 3:4 answers: “O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites, and of their children, which have sinned before thee”.

When we sin against God, God refers to us as dead. Remember the scripture says, keep my commandments and live. So Israelites living in sin are dead Israelites, even while they are walking around.

“And not hearkened unto the voice of thee their God: for the which cause these plagues cleave unto us.” That is why the plagues cleave unto us. One of those plagues is us going into slavery on ships: the transatlantic slave trade was a plague, one of the curses of Deuteronomy 28. Moses said we would go into tribulation again, this time by ships, and be sold to our enemies.

So the dead bodies lying in the street of the great city are the Israelites, spiritually dead, disconnected from our God, under the plagues that came because we did not hearken.

precepts.text: How happeneth it, Israel, that thou art in thine enemies' land, that thou art waxen old in a strange country, that thou art defiled with the dead? America is your enemies' land; our land is the land of Israel. Defiled with the dead means we walk around like zombies, breaking God's laws, confused about who we are.
precepts.point: The great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt: the same spirit that was in Sodom and Gomorrah, all that filth, is the same spirit here in America; and the same spirit that was in ancient Egypt, the oppression of the Israelites, is the same spirit here in America. That is why this place is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
Baruch goes on: “How happeneth it Israel, that thou art in thine enemies’ land”? Now we are in our enemies’ land. America is your enemies’ land; they are the ones ruling this place.

“That thou art waxen old in a strange country”: we have waxed old in strange countries, because our land is the land of Israel.

“That thou art defiled with the dead”. What does it mean that we are defiled with the dead? We walk around like zombies. We have broken God’s laws and we are living in these lands not knowing who we are. We are confused; we call ourselves all kinds of different names and titles. We are the congregation of the dead, the valley of dry bones. That is us today.

That is why Revelation 11:8 says “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”: the twelve tribes of Israel, spiritually dead, disconnected from God, lying in the streets of our enemies’ land.

precepts.text: He hath found out all the way of knowledge and given it to Jacob his servant and Israel his beloved; afterward he showed himself upon earth and conversed with men. All wisdom was given to us and our God walked with us, so there is no reason to sit on it.
precepts.point: It is two parts: the leader invites, and you accept. They straightway left their nets. Brothers sit in a chair while MOV, security, and kitchen call for help; you have followed every stat on league pass for thirteen years but do not know what the light is. Accept the invitation and at least show up to practice.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Christ walked by the sea of Galilee and said to Peter and Andrew, “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” Baruch shows where that invitation comes from.

“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” All the understanding and wisdom was given to us, not to the other nations. So there is no reason for you to sit on that wisdom and do nothing.

“Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.” That is speaking of Christ. We are the only ones that have a God; the other nations do not. Our God saw us as so special that he showed himself on the earth. Our God, Emmanuel, walked with us and conversed with us. That goes back to Matthew 4 when he said “Follow me”: that was our leader telling us to follow him.

So we are not supposed to just sit here and do absolutely nothing. Our God saw fit to walk with us, teach us and guide us, and we have to do the same thing: teach our brothers and sisters and wake them up. The invitation is there, and like Peter and Andrew, who “straightway left their nets, and followed him”, we have to accept it.

precepts.text: He hath found out all the way of knowledge and given it unto Jacob his servant.
precepts.point: Violence shall no more be heard in the land, and the people shall be all righteous.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” All the way of knowledge is the Bible. The Bible does not belong to all nations on earth; it was given only to the beloved Israelites.

That is who Peter is writing to: “This second epistle, beloved, I now write unto you”, to stir up their pure minds by way of remembrance, “That ye may be mindful of the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets”. The beloved of 2 Peter 3 is Israel his beloved of Baruch, the ones the way of knowledge was given to.

So when Peter warns “that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts”, he is warning the beloved about scoffers among them. Are we not seeing scoffers in these last days, like never before? Every black urban apologist is a scoffer. They don't believe the Bible. They don't believe Christ is black. They think Jesus is Caesar Borgia and the white man is coming to deliver them.

They say “Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.” Nothing has changed. But they “willingly are ignorant”, because we can take them to Deuteronomy and show them how things were prophesied and have come to pass, and it fits us perfect to a T. How are you going to say the Bible isn't a true book, when the knowledge in it was given to you?

precepts.text: We are yet this day in our captivity, subject to payments for the iniquities of our fathers.
precepts.point: We have given the hand to the Egyptians and the Assyrians to be satisfied with bread.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
Lamentations cries, “Remember, O Lord, what is come upon us: consider, and behold our reproach.” Baruch shows that the reproach is still upon us: “Behold, we are yet this day in our captivity, where thou hast scattered us, for a reproach and a curse, and to be subject to payments, according to all the iniquities of our fathers, which departed from the Lord our God.”

Lamentations goes on: “Our inheritance is turned to strangers, our houses to aliens.” “We have drunken our water for money; our wood is sold unto us.” You are seeing this now, in Cuba, in Venezuela, in parts of Africa. This isn't just for that time; don't tell us that was then, get over it. “We have given the hand to the Egyptians, and to the Assyrians, to be satisfied with bread”: we have given power, authority and sovereignty over our resources to Egypt and Assyria, to Babylon the Great, the United States, and to other nations. China is working its way into Latin America, and that is why Trump is getting more aggressive going over there now.

“Our fathers have sinned, and are not; and we have borne their iniquities.” The whole dynamic of the Monroe Doctrine, the Roosevelt Corollary and the big stick applies to the Northern Kingdom through that verse. We are still paying for the sins of our forefathers, bearing the brunt of it to this very day under all this oppression and economic violence. Chains don't have to be chains no more. Being here in America, we can't always fathom it, but it is not talking about any one person; it is the curse upon our people and our tribes.

“Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand.” The captivity now is economic. That is why Baruch says we are yet this day in our captivity, subject to payments. In the base form we say we have to pay taxes, and there is truth to that, but it is so much broader than that. And the key is at the end: “which departed from the Lord our God.”

This is the compassion we have to have to push this out to our people and speak to it properly: reach in, touch their soul, make it alive. Babylon speaks plainly; why aren't we? We have to rise up and fight that.

precepts.text: Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men: that is what the God of Israel did.
precepts.point: Christ is a God and angels are gods, but he is not a god the way a man is a god; he is the God of gods, and the disrespect is unreal.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

precepts.text: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach; the scattering did not end on a four hundred year clock.
precepts.point: Abram himself would go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age; and the seed would return in the fourth generation, for the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet full.

note.label: Genesis 15: The Covenant and the Four Hundred Years

precepts.why:
“Behold, we are yet this day in our captivity, where thou hast scattered us, for a reproach and a curse, and to be subject to payments, according to all the iniquities of our fathers, which departed from the Lord our God.”

Israel is still in captivity and still scattered this day. The northern kingdom’s captivity on this side began in 1492, and by that counting the years have passed four hundred and Israel is still not out. The scattering did not end on a four hundred year clock, which shows that Genesis 15:13 is not about America and 1619; that prophecy was fulfilled at the Exodus.

The twelve tribes scattered among the nations today, the people called Blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans, are the seed this covenant history belongs to, yet this day in their captivity for a reproach and subject to payments, according to the iniquities of our fathers.

precepts.text: We are yet this day in our captivity, scattered for a reproach, according to all the iniquities of our fathers which departed from the Lord our God.
precepts.point: Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

note.label: Exodus 20: The Ten Commandments

precepts.why:
An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast. Making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, “for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God”.

And he visits “the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me”. Baruch shows what that looks like: “Behold, we are yet this day in our captivity, where thou hast scattered us, for a reproach and a curse, and to be subject to payments, according to all the iniquities of our fathers, which departed from the Lord our God.”

Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers. That is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

precepts.text: The giants were men of great stature, famous from the beginning, yet destroyed because they had no wisdom.
precepts.point: The Lord had willed them to go up, but these men were so out of the spirit that they forgot He had already destroyed mightier nations before them. An evil report spreads a spirit of fear, but the Most High has not given His people the spirit of fear.

note.label: Numbers 13: The Spies Search the Land

precepts.why:
The spies said, “there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.” Baruch tells what became of the giants.

“There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war. Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them: But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.”

Men of great stature, famous and expert in war, and the Lord destroyed them anyway, because they had no wisdom. The Lord had already destroyed mightier nations before Israel, and the ten spies forgot it and feared the sons of Anak instead of believing the God who willed them to go up.

precepts.text: The giants the people feared perished through their own foolishness, for the Lord chose them not.
precepts.point: The giants were famous from the beginning, of great stature and expert in war, yet the Lord chose them not and gave them no knowledge; they were destroyed because they had no wisdom and perished through their own foolishness. There are no giants today; stature and skill in war saved none of them.

note.label: Deuteronomy 2: Meddle Not With Them, and the Giants That Perished

precepts.why:
Ammon's land also was accounted a land of giants, the Zamzummims, “A people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims; but the Lord destroyed them before them”. Baruch tells why they perished: “There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war. Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them: But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.”

The giants the people feared were famous from the beginning, of great stature and expert in war, yet the Lord chose them not and gave them no knowledge. Stature and skill in war saved none of them; they were destroyed because they had no wisdom, and the Ammonites succeeded them and dwelt in their stead.

There are no giants today.

precepts.text: We are yet this day in our captivity, subject unto payments for the iniquities of our fathers; we have to obey the laws of the land under the hand of our oppressor, endure, and exercise faith in the keeping of the commandments until Christ redeems us.
precepts.point: They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water shall rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord. That is where we are right now: in the places of drawing water, rehearsing the righteous acts of the Most High while the arrows are still being shot.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
“They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water, there shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord.” That is where we are right now: in the places of drawing water, rehearsing the righteous acts of the Most High while the arrows are still being shot.

Baruch describes our position: “Behold, we are yet this day in our captivity, where thou hast scattered us, for a reproach and a curse, and to be subject to payments, according to all the iniquities of our fathers, which departed from the Lord our God.”

We are yet this day in our captivity, subject unto payments for the iniquities of our fathers. So we have to obey the laws of the land under the hand of our oppressor, endure, and exercise faith in the keeping of the commandments until Christ redeems us. Then, delivered from the noise of the archers, the people of the Lord go down to the gates.

precepts.text: If our forefathers had walked in the way of the Most High they would have dwelled in peace forever, which shows we are the ones under the curses, because right now we are not living in a time of peace.
precepts.point: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep; for thou, Lord, only makest me to dwell in safety. Safety comes from the Most High, and it comes by keeping His statutes and judgments.

note.label: Psalm 4: The Lord Hath Set Apart Him That Is Godly for Himself

precepts.why:
“Thou hast forsaken the fountain of wisdom. For if thou hadst walked in the way of God, thou shouldest have dwelled in peace for ever.” If our forefathers had walked in the way of the Most High, they would have dwelled in peace for ever. They did not, and that shows we are the ones under the curses, because right now we are not living in a time of peace.

David lay down in peace and slept because the Lord made him dwell in safety, and that safety is tied to doing the statutes and judgments. Forsake the fountain of wisdom, and the peace goes with it. “There be many that say, Who will shew us any good?” The good, the gladness in the heart greater than the increase of corn and wine, comes when the Most High lifts up the light of his countenance upon us, and that is by walking in his way.

precepts.text: Israel is the beloved of the Bible, and this is our God, the God of our forefathers.
precepts.point: Moab is His washpot, the servant, and over Edom He casts out His shoe, treating Edom as a slave to clean His shoes.

note.label: Psalm 108: My Heart Is Fixed

precepts.why:
“That thy beloved may be delivered”. Baruch tells who the beloved is: “This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.”

Israel is the beloved of the Bible. And this is our God, the God of our forefathers, who found out all the way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob his servant. So the deliverance David prays for is the deliverance of Israel.

precepts.text: Israel is the beloved; the Most High hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.
precepts.point: For so he giveth his beloved sleep. He gives the Israelites rest, rest from the bread of sorrows.

note.label: Psalm 127: Except the Lord Build the House

precepts.why:
“for so he giveth his beloved sleep.” Israel is the beloved: the Most High hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved. “Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.”

He gives the Israelites rest, rest from the bread of sorrows. It is vain to rise up early and sit up late to eat the bread of sorrows, vain to labor and build without the apostles, the prophets, and Christ as our leader; the rest is given to his beloved.

precepts.text: We forsook the fountain of wisdom; had we walked in his way we would have dwelt in peace forever.
precepts.point: When we apply righteousness we will be at peace among each other; this is the peace Christ and Paul preached among the brethren. Even our forefathers understood in captivity that walking in the way of God brings peace.

note.label: Isaiah 32: A King Shall Reign in Righteousness

precepts.why:
“And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness quietness and assurance for ever.” Even our forefathers understood this in captivity: “How happeneth it Israel, that thou art in thine enemies’ land, that thou art waxen old in a strange country, that thou art defiled with the dead, That thou art counted with them that go down into the grave? Thou hast forsaken the fountain of wisdom. For if thou hadst walked in the way of God, thou shouldest have dwelled in peace for ever.”

We forsook the fountain of wisdom; that is how we came to be in our enemies’ land, waxen old in a strange country. Had we walked in his way we would have dwelt in peace forever. That is the same peace Isaiah speaks of, the work of righteousness. When we apply righteousness we will be at peace among each other, the peace Christ and Paul preached among the brethren, and it lasts “Until the spirit be poured upon us from on high”, when judgment dwells in the wilderness and righteousness remains in the fruitful field.

precepts.text: He hath given the way of knowledge unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved. That names who the beloved are.
precepts.point: But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
Baruch says, “This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him”. Then he names the ones God gave his knowledge to: “He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.”

That names who the beloved are. When John writes “Beloved, now are we the sons of God”, the beloved are Jacob his servant, Israel his beloved. The way of knowledge was given to Israel, and it is those who received him, who believe on his name, that are given power to become the sons of God.
